summary.summary: Arun ended 2025/26 with £35.46m of PWLB debt — four maturity loans taken in 2012 for HRA housing self-financing at an average 3.40%, the first not repayable until 2030 — against a capital financing requirement of £52.06m, leaving £16.6m covered by internal cash instead of loans. No new borrowing was taken during the year, and planned borrowing-funded capital spending largely did not happen (£2.956m unfinanced capital expenditure against an original £27.913m), so the CFR barely moved. Investment income was £2.3m against a £2.02m budget on average balances of about £53m. The council's two CCLA pooled funds are worth £559k less than the £7m put in — a loss parked behind the IFRS 9 statutory override until March 2029, with a £500k equalisation reserve set aside against it.

signals.headline: Verified quiet: no new borrowing in 2025/26; £35.46m HRA PWLB debt (first maturity 28/3/2030) against £52.06m CFR; investment income £275k over budget
signals.why: An under-borrowed district with a fixed, distant-maturity debt book and returns beating budget presents no near-term treasury concern.

news_drafts.headline: Arun's housing survey data too flawed to guide £30m investment plan
news_drafts.lead: Arun Council's stock condition survey, which underpins its 30-year housing investment strategy, has been rated as unreliable by its external consultant. The survey, which assessed 3,430 properties, used non-standard scoring with no written guidance to surveyors, different versions with undocumented changes, and no quality assurance. Three different companies conducted surveys with inconsistent results. A quarter of the stock—681 properties and 103 blocks—remains unsurveyed. The consultant's report to the Housing and Wellbeing Committee states the data "lacks proper documentation, quality assurance, and consistency across suppliers" and that extensive additional work is needed before the council can plan investment accurately. The survey also excludes communal elements, balconies and garages for which the council is financially responsible, meaning investment costs are significantly understated. The council's reported Decent Homes compliance of 42 per cent cannot be relied upon for either compliance reporting or investment planning.

news_drafts.headline: Arun Council's budget plans may need to account for local government restructuring
news_drafts.lead: Arun Council's chief finance officer has flagged that the council's budget proposals may need to be reassessed in light of possible local government reorganisation — a potential restructuring that could reshape how councils operate. The Section 151 Officer, who has a legal duty to warn if the council cannot balance its books, raised the concern during budget planning. The officer provided no details on timing, likelihood, or form. The flag suggests that local government reorganisation could be in prospect, though no formal announcement has been made.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report - Appendix A
findings.headline: Multiple recent audits with Limited/No assurance opinions showing non-responsive management action follow-up
findings.detail: National Non-Domestic Rates (Limited opinion, January 2026) management action due 28.02.26 received no responses to chases on 20/05/26, 04/06/26, 01/07/26 and 11/08/26. Housing Statutory Health & Safety (Limited opinion, July 2026) high-priority actions due 31.07.26 provided no response to follow-up dated 11/08/26. Responsive Repairs (No opinion, July 2026) high-priority actions due June-August 2026 similarly unresponsive to 11/08/26 follow-up. Asset Management (Limited opinion, May 2024) high-priority action for implementing Civica database was originally due 30.06.25, revised to 31.05.26, and remains ongoing. The pattern of non-response across multiple service areas from spring 2026 onwards suggests either resource constraints affecting management's capacity to respond to audit follow-ups, or prioritization of audit actions below competing pressures.
findings.matters: A finance director or lender monitoring governance needs to understand management's responsiveness to audit findings and capacity to remediate identified control weaknesses; consistency of non-response across reviews indicates systemic issue
findings.figures: 4 NNDR chases with no response spanning 20/05 to 11/08/26; Multiple audits with no response to 11/08/26 follow-up
findings.quote: Update was requested from the service on 11/08/26; however, no response has been received to date.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report - Appendix A
findings.headline: National Non-Domestic Rates audit received Limited assurance opinion with £19.3m aged arrears and collection process delays
findings.detail: As at 30 September 2025, NNDR arrears stood at £19,327,556.53 with 69.4% (£13,404,886.80) aged 6-12 months, indicating bills from prior year or early current year remain unpaid. Previous year (2024-25) arrears recorded November 2025 totalled £870,281.77 with £424,952.17 aged 6-12 months and £59,944.52 over 12 months. Review of outstanding debt 2010-2024 identified £30,290 requiring write-off for deceased or insolvent businesses, and found £14,383.54 owed by Arun District Council itself and £2,495 owed by West Sussex County Council. Audit notes historic resource shortage in recovery function addressed by appointment of two Recovery Officers. Management action due 28.02.26 (now overdue) received no responses to follow-up requests dated 20/05/26, 04/06/26, 01/07/26 and 11/08/26.
findings.matters: NNDR is material income to the council; aged debt and collection delays affect cashflow and financial sustainability
findings.figures: £19,327,556.53 arrears at 30.09.25; £13,404,886.80 (69.4%) aged 6-12 months; £30,290 requiring write-off; £14,383.54 council's own debt
findings.quote: The presence of aged debt beyond 12 months and large sums at Final Notice stage highlight delays in escalation and potential weaknesses in recovery processes.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report - Appendix A
findings.headline: Contract Management audit received Limited assurance opinion with register accuracy gaps and inconsistent contractor due diligence and monitoring
findings.detail: The council has effective arrangements including hosted contract register through In-Tend system and updated Constitution approved November 2025. However, contract register accuracy requires improvement, limiting reliability of management information and oversight. Arrangements for ongoing contractor due diligence and monitoring are not consistently defined or applied, resulting in variable evidence of compliance. Contract performance reviews and meetings lack uniform documentation and consistency. Contract management training availability exists but expectations regarding attendance and evidence of uptake are unclear. The audit identified 11 high-priority management actions.
findings.matters: Contract governance and vendor due diligence directly affect value-for-money, financial control and risk management across council expenditure
findings.figures: 11 high-priority management actions identified and agreed
findings.quote: The accuracy of the contract register requires improvement, which in its current state, limits the reliability of management information and oversight. In addition, arrangements for ongoing contractor due diligence and monitoring are not consistently defined or applied, resulting in variable evidence of compliance across contracts.

findings.paper_title: Internal Audit Progress Report - Appendix A
findings.headline: Housing Responsive Repairs audit found 46.7% completion within timeframe, 90% of tested repairs non-compliant with procurement rules, and 54 job reconciliation mismatches
findings.detail: The audit identified 54 repair jobs recorded in the Propellor work management system not present in Civica CX, indicating unreliable weekly system reconciliation. Of 2,226 repairs recorded to September 2025, only 1,040 (46.7%) were completed within required timeframe; 229 (10.2%) were completed late; 332 (15%) open cases had missed deadline; 513 (23%) had no deadline set. Testing of 20 repairs by external suppliers found 18 (90%) non-compliant with Contract Standing Orders: 15 had one quote when two were required; 2 had no quotes; 1 had two quotes from same supplier. All 20 tested repairs lacked required pre and post-work photographic evidence. Multiple high-priority management actions due June-August 2026 show no progress; follow-up requests sent 11/08/26 received no response.
findings.matters: Housing repairs represent material expenditure and asset management; No assurance indicates fundamental control breakdown in contractor selection, work quality oversight and financial management
findings.figures: 46.7% completion within timeframe; 90% (18/20) non-compliant with procurement rules; 54 job reconciliation mismatches; 23% repairs with no deadline set
findings.quote: Of the 20 cases tested, 18 were found to be non‑compliant.

findings.headline: Emergency repairs completion rate falls 18 percentage points below target in single quarter
findings.detail: Emergency repair completion within timescale fell to 80.12% this quarter from 98.83% previous quarter, well below 95% target. Manager notes remaining overdue repairs are increasingly complex. Daily monitoring and contractor KPIs are in place to manage.
findings.matters: Sharp performance deterioration may indicate contractor issues or resource constraints; complexity of outstanding repairs suggests potential cost pressures.
findings.figures: 80.12% of 387 emergency repairs completed within timescale (target 95%), down from 98.83% previous quarter
